summary: Self-named off-registry HTTPS dependency delivers arbitrary code at install time
details: package.json declares a dependency whose key equals the package's own name, ring-device-settings-library, and whose value is the off-registry HTTPS URL https://repo.securityctrl.com/ring-device-settings-library. On npm install, npm fetches whatever bytes that host returns and installs them — including any lifecycle scripts — with no version pin and no integrity check. The manifest line itself is the delivery mechanism: whoever controls repo.securityctrl.com controls code executed on the installer's machine. The dependency-confusion shape (dependency key matches the package name) and the implausibly high version (30.0.0) are consistent with an internal-name-squat intended to win resolution against a private package of the same name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
